translation automation technology offers a transformative approach to advancing global health equity by overcoming linguistic barriers in low-resource regions. This study examines the potential of fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) to improve automated medical translation for underrepresented languages, with a focus on Chinese-to-Hindi translation. Leveraging a parallel medical text corpus, we iteratively fine-tuned ChatGPT and compared its performance with that of a traditional dual-input LSTM model. Results demonstrate that fine-tuning significantly improves translation quality, with BLEU scores increasing from 14.48 to 17.66 and chrF++ scores from 39.19 to 42.14, outperforming both the baseline model and Google\u2019s translation service. The iterative fine-tuning process further enhanced linguistic accuracy, particularly for complex medical terminology. In contrast, the LSTM model achieved only modest performance (BLEU: 0.23, chrF++: 7.58), highlighting the superiority of LLM-based approaches in low-resource settings. These findings highlight the potential of translation automation technology to bridge linguistic gaps in healthcare communication, although challenges remain in terms of scalability, cultural adaptation, and computational demands.
